findings: FINDING tests/test_a_model_launches_with_its_declared_settings.py:275 follow-on: rows is keyed by the model name (rows[settings.get("model")] = dict(settings)) and read back at line 301 as rows[row.model], so two offered rows that ever carry the same model name would mispair one row's settings against another row's dispatch, and the guard would either fail spuriously or leave one row unverified; keying by the backend and model key the row names would make it robust.
